china-1922:p0310_2.rationale: Balance sheet of the Bank of China 1917-19 with liabilities and assets: capital, deposits, loans and notes in circulation.

china-1922:p0312_1.rationale: List of officers of the Bank of Communications (name, position, province); textual roster with no quantities. Bank is a government bank, but the table is a personnel list and no tag fits cleanly.
review_questions: Consider a tag for bank personnel or officers; government-offices does not clearly fit a bank roster.

china-1922:p0313_1.rationale: Balance sheet of the Bank of Communications 1917-19 with capital, deposits, notes, loans and investments.

china-1922:p0314_1.rationale: Decimal subdivision of the tael into mace, candareens and cash; a monetary unit equivalence table.

china-1922:p0315_1.rationale: Haikwan tael equivalents at average sight exchange on London, New York, Paris and other centres, 1910-1920.

china-1922:p0316_1.rationale: Approximate exchange values between different kinds of taels (Kuping, Haikwan, local taels at treaty ports); conversions between monetary units within China rather than between national currencies.
review_questions: Is a tag for monetary unit equivalence or measurement-and-units appropriate for tael conversions?

china-1922:p0318_1.rationale: Monthly percentage of new, mostly light-weight coins in Shanghai tramway receipts, a measure of subsidiary coin circulation. Tramway is only the source of the receipts.

china-1922:p0319_1.rationale: Minting costs, face value, depreciation and minting profit on 1-cent and 2-cent copper coins; subsidiary coinage.

china-1922:p0320_1.rationale: Depreciation level at which minting profits on 1-cent and 2-cent copper coins would disappear; face versus intrinsic value of subsidiary coins.

china-1922:p0320_2.rationale: Monthly depreciation of copper 1-cent coins in Shanghai, expressed as number per dollar, 1919-1921.
